# 0.0.0-dev.1: ???? (??-??-????)

## Breaking changes

- regurgitate now requires Quarto 1.10 or later.

## Features

- `regurgitate` creates a "Code Appendix" at the end of your document containing all code blocks.
- Configuration options:
  - `group-by-language`: Group code blocks in appendix by programming language.
  - `show-code-inline`: Control whether code remains inline or is removed.
  - `show-output-results`: Control whether execution results are included in appendix.
- Supports multiple programming languages (Python, R, Julia, etc.).

## Bug fixes

- `appendix-level` now sets the level of the appendix heading. Previously, the
  heading was always level 1.
- `show-code-inline: false` now removes only the code that moves to the
  appendix. Cell outputs stay in place, including those of `echo: false` cells,
  and code marked `appendix: false` stays inline. Previously, whole cells
  disappeared from the document, outputs included.
- regurgitate now collects code blocks and cells inside callouts, tabsets and
  columns, and `show-code-inline: false` removes their code there too.
  Previously, only top-level code reached the appendix.
- Cells and code blocks with a `filename` now appear in the appendix, labeled
  with their filename when `show-filename` is on. Previously, they were left out.

## Documentation

- The README, home page and FAQ no longer say that regurgitate has only three or
  four options.
